facts: The paper introduces KAZE features, a novel multiscale 2D feature detection and description algorithm in nonlinear scale spaces.
Previous approaches detect and describe features at different scale levels by building or approximating the Gaussian scale space of an image.
Gaussian blurring does not respect the natural boundaries of objects.
Gaussian blurring smoothes to the same degree both details and noise.
Gaussian blurring reduces localization accuracy and distinctiveness.
2D features are detected and described in a nonlinear scale space by means of nonlinear diffusion filtering.
Blurring can be made locally adaptive to the image data.
Locally adaptive blurring retains object boundaries.
Locally adaptive blurring obtains superior localization accuracy and distinctiviness.
The nonlinear scale space is built using efficient Additive Operator Splitting (AOS) techniques and variable con-ductance diffusion.
An extensive evaluation on benchmark datasets is presented.
A practical matching application on deformable surfaces is presented.
KAZE features are somewhat more expensive to compute than SURF due to the construction of the nonlinear scale space.
KAZE features are comparable to SIFT.
entities: multiscale 2D feature detection and description algorithm
